Description: Distribution and Core functions are merged into a single Layer 3 switch/router pair, connected directly to Access Switches.
Pros: Lowest cost, low configuration complexity, sufficient performance for SME scale (~150 users).
Cons: Limited expansion capacity if scaling beyond multi-building campus.
Suitability_For_SME: HIGHLY RECOMMENDED (Optimal balance for 150 users, 3-floor building).

Description: Dedicated Core layer switches connecting separate Distribution layer switch pairs, which then aggregate Access switches.
Pros: Maximum modularity and scalability across large multi-building campuses.
Cons: Over-engineered for a single 3-floor building, high hardware cost, excessive management overhead.
Suitability_For_SME: OVERKILL (Unnecessary complexity and cost for current scale).

Architecture_Option: Option 3: Routed Access Layer (L3 to Access)
Description: Layer 3 routing boundaries pushed directly down to edge Access Switches, eliminating Layer 2 trunks.
Pros: Eliminates Spanning-Tree loops completely, fastest convergence times.
Cons: Requires expensive Layer 3 access switches, prevents Layer 2 adjacency across floors if needed.
Suitability_For_SME: MODERATE (Higher switch cost, restricts L2 flexibility).
